question.text: Will the Detroit Red Wings beat the Florida Panthers in their November 12, 2026 game?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the Detroit Red Wings are the winning team in their NHL regular-season game against the Florida Panthers scheduled for Thursday, November 12, 2026 (7:30 p.m. ET) at Amerant Bank Arena in Sunrise, Florida. The result is read from the official final score on the NHL's scores page for that date: https://www.nhl.com/scores/2026-11-12. A win in regulation, overtime, or a shootout all resolve YES; a loss in regulation, overtime, or a shootout all resolve NO. If that page is unavailable or does not show this game, the result shown for this game on the Red Wings' official schedule page (https://www.nhl.com/redwings/schedule) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: If the game is postponed, suspended, or otherwise not completed by 11:59 p.m. ET on November 12, 2026, this question resolves as Annulled.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The game is on Nov. 12, 2026, about 10 days from now, and the result will be known that night (around 03:00 UTC on Nov. 13). For YES, Detroit must beat Florida in Sunrise, whether in regulation, overtime or a shootout.

(b) There is no status quo outcome for a game not yet played. The default expectation is that Florida, the home team and the stronger, deeper club, is favored.

(c) Base rate: NHL road teams win about 45-47% of games. Road underdogs priced like Detroit here (+145 to +155) win about 38-40% of the time. The closest market, Kalshi's line for the same matchup at the same venue on Nov. 2, gives Detroit 39%.

(d) Evidence for each side:
- **For YES:**
  - Florida is still missing Barkov (out to about Nov. 27) and Marchand (out to about Nov. 21) for the Nov. 12 game.
  - Florida had uneven stretches in late October, including being outscored 9-1 in two losses.
  - Detroit may get Appleton (about Nov. 10) and Johansson (about Nov. 5) back.
  - Both teams play their second game in three nights, so neither has a rest edge.
- **For NO:**
  - Larkin is suspended indefinitely (Oct. 29), and Kasper is out to about Nov. 14.
  - Edvinsson is absent in a contract dispute.
  - Detroit's penalty kill ranks 27th (68.9%), while Florida's power play leads the league in expected goals for (Covers, Nov. 2).
  - Florida has the league's lowest 5-on-5 expected goals against.
  - Florida has won four of the last five head-to-head meetings.
  - Markstrom may be back in Florida's net.

(e) Scenarios:
- **NO:** Florida's power play punishes Detroit's weak penalty kill, Markstrom or Schmid holds firm, and Florida wins 4-2.
- **YES:** Gibson steals the game, and Detroit takes advantage of a thin Florida lineup without Barkov and Marchand to win in overtime or a shootout.

(f) I anchor on the 39% Kalshi price for the near-identical Nov. 2 game. Conditions on Nov. 12 look largely the same: same venue, Florida's injured players still out, and the Larkin situation unresolved. A Larkin trade, the Nov. 2 result, or a change in goalie could shift this slightly, but these risks are roughly balanced. I adjust slightly downward to reflect general uncertainty and Florida's head-to-head edge, landing at about 38%.
